prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Technical Drawing, acquired in previous stages of education (High School and Vocational Training).
Basic user-level computer skills, both with the Windows environment and applications. Handling digital files in a computer environment.

Basic user-level browser usage for accessing the virtual platform or online teaching-learning resources that, where applicable, the University of Salamanca makes available to the university community.

learning_outcomes.text: Develop spatial vision and the ability to see, represent, and objectively express three-dimensional forms on a plane.
Provide students with different resources and strategies for representation on a plane, using various graphic methods and codes to create the sensation of depth on the plane.
Knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Know and learn the possibilities of Computer-Aided Design as a tool for Graphic Expression in Engineering, and its applications to Engineering Design and Projects.
Ability to relate the aforementioned applied knowledge with those of the different scientific disciplines typical of other subjects in their study plan.
Understanding and interpreting texts and data, developing skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the field of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, which enhance aptitudes for developing own initiatives and undertaking new projects.
Spatial vision capacity and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.

assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average of Block I (Drawing, 2/3 weight) and Block II (CAD, 1/3 weight). A minimum grade of 3.5 out of 10 is required in each block and each part to be eligible for compensation. For the second sitting, grades of 5 out of 10 or higher for individual blocks or parts are carried over. The second sitting consists of a single comprehensive exam for Block I (weighted as 40% Diédrico, 33% Normalización, 27% Acotados) and a single comprehensive exam for Block II (100% CAD).
